briefdescription.para: Compute the axisymmetric B-operator (4 components).
Compute the B̄-operator using the B-bar selective-reduced-integration method.
Compute the Green–Lagrange strain operator for deformation gradient F.
Compute the expanded interpolation operator N_B from shape function values N.
Compute the element Jacobian from natural derivatives dNdXi and the stored nodal coordinates.
Compute physical derivatives dN/dX from natural derivatives and the inverse Jacobian.
Compute the deformation gradient $\mathbf{F}$ from physical derivatives and displacements Q.
The physical coordinates of the element center, the image of the centroid of the reference domain.

The characteristic element length $L_e$ at the natural coordinates xi, for the stable time increment $\Delta t = f\, L_e / c$ of explicit dynamics, with the wave speed $c$ and a factor $f$ for the lumped mass distribution (see MassLumping::timeStepFactorFromMassDistribution).

listitem.para: Quadrilateral, hexahedron and line: $L_e = 2\,\sigma_\mathrm{min}(\mathbf{J})$, twice the smallest singular value of the Jacobian. The Jacobian maps the cube $[-1,1]^{n_\mathrm{dim}}$ onto the element, so this is the element's smallest physical extent.

Linear simplex: $L_e = 1 / \sqrt{\sum_i |\nabla N_i|^2} = 1 / \sqrt{\sum_i h_i^{-2}}$, with the constant shape function gradients $\nabla N_i$ and the altitude $h_i$ opposite node $i$. Unlike the Jacobian of the unit simplex, it does not depend on the node numbering.

detaileddescription.para: Quadratic simplices (Tri6, Tetra10) have no derived length; using one is a compile error.

parameterdescription.para: Natural coordinates; irrelevant for a linear simplex, whose gradients are constant.

briefdescription.para: The natural coordinates of the centroid of the reference domain: the origin of the cube [-1, 1]^nDim, ( 1 / ( nDim + 1 ), ... ) for the unit simplex.
The volume-equivalent length $(V_\mathrm{ref} \det\mathbf{J})^{1/n_\mathrm{dim}}$: the side of the square or cube with the measure the element would have if its Jacobian were detJ everywhere.

detaileddescription.para: $V_\mathrm{ref}$ is the measure of the reference domain (getReferenceMeasure()): 2, 4 and 8 for the line and the cubes $[-1,1]^{n_\mathrm{dim}}$, 1/2 and 1/6 for the unit triangle and tetrahedron, for elements of any order on that domain. For an element with straight edges $\det\mathbf{J}$ is constant and this is exactly $\sqrt{A}$ or $\sqrt[3]{V}$; for a curved or distorted one it is the measure the element would have with the Jacobian at that point. Elements pass it to their materials as the regularisation length of softening laws.

parameterdescription.para: Determinant of the Jacobian, e.g. at a quadrature point.

briefdescription.para: Statically-sized geometry base class for all isoparametric Marmot elements.

detaileddescription.para:
nDim
Number of spatial dimensions (1, 2 or 3).
nNodes
Number of element nodes.
Provides shape functions N, their natural-coordinate derivatives dNdXi, the B-operator B, and the element Jacobian. The element shape is determined automatically from the template parameters.
Concrete Marmot::Discretizations::Elements::Element classes inherit from this class to access the geometric infrastructure without code duplication.
